subsystems.name: Tube and vacuum system
subsystems.role: holds a low-pressure environment so pods face almost no air resistance.
parts: vacuum pumps spaced along the route

subsystems.name: Pod
subsystems.role: carries passengers or cargo at high speed inside the tube.

subsystems.name: Levitation and propulsion
subsystems.role: lifts the pod off the track and accelerates it without contact.
parts: linear motor stator along the tube

subsystems.name: Power and control
subsystems.role: supplies electricity and manages pod movement safely.

subsystems.name: Stations and terminals
subsystems.role: let people and cargo enter and leave without losing the vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Select and survey the route
buildSteps.detail: Engineers map terrain, geology and land ownership, because the tube must run straight and level for hundreds of kilometres.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate tube segments
buildSteps.detail: Steel or prestressed concrete sections are manufactured in a factory to tight tolerances, with internal rails or guideways already fitted.

buildSteps.title: Build foundations and supports
buildSteps.detail: Pylons are erected above ground, or tunnels are bored, to carry the tube and keep it aligned.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and align the tube
buildSteps.detail: Segments are welded or bolted together, then laser-aligned to within millimetres over long distances.

buildSteps.title: Install the vacuum system
buildSteps.detail: Pumps are connected at intervals and seals are tested to hold a pressure about a thousandth of atmospheric.

buildSteps.title: Lay the levitation and motor track
buildSteps.detail: Maglev coils and linear motor windings are installed along the entire tube and wired to power supplies.

buildSteps.title: Build and test the pod
buildSteps.detail: A lightweight composite pod is assembled with its levitation skids, linear motor reaction plate and life support, then tested on a short track.

buildSteps.title: Commission the system
buildSteps.detail: The tube is pumped down and the pod is run at increasing speed, first uncrewed, then with crew, before any passengers are carried.

prerequisites.why: proven in high-speed trains and test tracks, but must be adapted to work inside a vacuum.
particle accelerators maintain good vacuum over kilometres, but keeping it over hundreds of kilometres with pods moving through is untested.
aerospace and racing industries build strong, light cabins that can hold pressure.

prerequisites.tech: Pod life support and emergency systems
prerequisites.why: spacecraft life support exists, but rapid evacuation from a sealed tube at speed is unsolved.
signalling must manage pods at over 1,000 km/h with braking distances of many kilometres.

pathway.milestone: subscale test tracks demonstrate levitation and low-speed travel in partial vacuum
pathway.unlocks: proof that the basic physics and components work together.

pathway.milestone: full-scale pod tests at several hundred km/h on a few-kilometre track
pathway.unlocks: data on vibration, thermal expansion and vacuum maintenance.

pathway.milestone: first commercial route, likely for freight on a short, dedicated corridor
pathway.unlocks: revenue operation and public confidence without carrying passengers.

pathway.milestone: passenger networks linking cities hundreds of kilometres apart
pathway.unlocks: very fast ground transport — if safety, cost and political will align.
